description: Strip HTML comments outside script/style blocks, conditional comments preserved. Pure representation; expect ~1.9 kB.

Remove CSS rules whose selector names a class/id that appears nowhere else in the file (markup, attributes AND script text all count as 'present', so JS-toggled classes survive). Conservative static reachability, per-page.

Drop leading indentation and blank lines inside <style> only. One declaration still per line, so the CSS stays readable and diffable; this is the half of minification that costs nothing in maintainability.

PROBE, expect the score to improve and the change to be rejected anyway: collapse all whitespace around { ; : , inside <style>. Tests whether the remaining CSS bytes are reachable only through full minification. If it scores, the question is no longer 'can we' but 'should we' - a single-line 10 kB blob is not diffable or hand-editable, and these are hand-maintained client pages.
Strip indentation, blank lines and whole-line // comments inside inline <script>. Line-oriented only: intra-line spacing untouched, so no ASI hazard and no string-literal damage.

Collapse markup indentation only in the safe position: a whitespace run that sits entirely between '>' and '<'. pre/textarea/style/script excluded, and inter-word whitespace inside text nodes is never touched, so no rendered spacing changes.

PROBE CONFIRMED, discarding: guard-text-preserved failed the section deletion exactly as predicted (logs/r7-guard1.log names faq.html DRIFT), while validate-html passed it. Section restored to the r6 state; back to baseline score, so this journals as a non-improvement. The anti-content-deletion floor is live in this run, not just in unit tests.
